h1: Quartier by Montraj — a peaceful boutique just three minutes from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital
intro: Tucked into the quiet dead-end of Soi Sukhumvit 49/11, barely 200 metres from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital, Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit is a 4-star boutique that opened in 2022 with French-contemporary styling and a residential calm unusual for Bangkok hotels. Ninety-four rooms, a 10th-floor pool and the intimate Cul de Sac rooftop bar make it feel more like a stylish apartment block than a hotel — which is exactly the point. The walk to the hospital takes under three minutes; reaching BTS Phrom Phong requires a 10–12 minute Grab ride. Rooms start from approx. THB 1,500/night, with a score of 8.7 from 310 reviews on Trip.com and 8.3 from 918 reviews on Booking.com.

body.html: The name Quartier means 'neighbourhood' in French, and the hotel leans fully into that identity — it sits inside a genuine cul-de-sac off Soi 49, which also gives the rooftop bar its name: Cul de Sac. The Montraj Hotels group opened this property in 2022 as a deliberately low-key retreat in one of central Bangkok's quietest residential pockets, while keeping it within easy reach of the area's main practical landmark: Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital, about 200 metres away along Soi 49.

The 94 rooms fall into three tiers. Cozy Twin (23 sqm) works for two guests sharing single beds but is genuinely compact. Quartier King (27 sqm) is the most popular option and feels comfortable for a couple. Deluxe King (32 sqm) adds floor-to-ceiling windows, an extra seating corner and a noticeably more generous floor plan. All rooms include a fridge, air-conditioning, TV and free Wi-Fi. The recurring gripe across platforms is that the smaller room categories feel undersized for a 4-star rating, so if size matters to you, book Deluxe King from the outset.
"Staff super nice and supportive, rooftop bar has amazing atmosphere. Beds are seriously comfortable — one of the best I've slept in during my Bangkok trip."

The category where Quartier genuinely earns its stars is staff service. Booking.com guests rate it 9.0 and Trip.com guests 8.8 — both well above the Bangkok average for this price tier. Cleanliness is similarly strong at 9.0 on Trip.com. The Cul de Sac rooftop bar draws consistent praise for its intimate atmosphere and creative cocktails, a pleasant wind-down after a long hospital day. Breakfast earns good marks for variety.

The location is a genuine trade-off. For hospital visits it is unbeatable — a straight three-minute walk to Samitivej Sukhumvit's main entrance, no vehicle needed. For everything else in Bangkok, you are in a residential dead-end with no public transport at the door. BTS Phrom Phong is around 850 m away via a route that isn't particularly pleasant to walk in Bangkok's heat; most guests call a Grab (10–12 minutes, roughly THB 80–100). Nearby amenities include a Villa Market supermarket, Japanese restaurants and local cafés along Soi 49.

Honest notes from reading through the reviews: a few guests report a faint musty smell in hallways or certain rooms, and some mention towels that look older than the hotel. The hotel entrance is hidden inside the parking lot, which confuses first-time arrivals — save the exact pin in Google Maps before you come. Wi-Fi speed is inconsistent according to some reviews. Free parking is available, a genuine plus if you are driving yourself or accompanying a patient.

The bottom line: Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit earns its place as the most convenient hotel for Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital among the options in this roundup. It is quiet, clean, the staff are warm, and the nightly rate is fair for the neighbourhood. The caveats — no BTS walkability, modest room sizes in the lower categories, and occasional humidity issues — are real, but unlikely to bother someone whose primary reason for being here is the hospital next door.

honestSummary: Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit is the right call if your trip revolves around Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital — the three-minute walk is hard to beat and nothing else in the immediate cluster comes close. Staff quality and cleanliness punch above the price point. The trade-offs — no walkable BTS access, compact lower-category rooms and occasional humidity issues — are real but manageable, especially for guests who are here for medical reasons rather than sightseeing.
honestChecks: If you plan to use the BTS every day — BTS Phrom Phong is 850 m away with no direct public transport; you will need a Grab each time → consider a hotel closer to a BTS station if transit convenience is your priority.

If you expect spacious rooms — Cozy Twin (23 sqm) and Quartier King (27 sqm) are compact for a 4-star; genuinely small storage space → upgrade to Deluxe King (32 sqm) or ask to inspect the room at check-in.
If you are sensitive to odours — a handful of reviews note a musty or damp smell in hallways and some rooms → report it to reception straight away; the staff here are known for responding quickly.

tips.title: Walk to Samitivej Sukhumvit in 3 minutes
tips.body: Leave the hotel and walk west along Soi 49 — the hospital entrance (133 Soi Sukhumvit 49) is roughly 200 metres away. No vehicle needed at any time of day.

tips.title: Use Grab to reach BTS Phrom Phong
tips.body: No public transport runs directly past the hotel. A Grab to BTS Phrom Phong takes 10–12 minutes and costs around THB 80–100 depending on the time of day.

tips.title: Save the pin before you arrive
tips.body: The hotel entrance is inside the parking lot and easy to miss on your first visit. Save the Google Maps pin in advance or call the hotel — they are happy to guide you in by phone.

tips.title: Travelling with a pet
tips.body: Quartier by Montraj is pet-friendly. Confirm the pet policy and any additional charges directly with the hotel when booking — conditions may vary by pet size.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit

faq.q: How far is Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is at 413 Soi Sukhumvit 49/11. Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital (133 Soi Sukhumvit 49) is approximately 200 metres away — a 2–3 minute walk along Soi 49. No vehicle is needed. This makes it the closest hotel to the hospital in the recommended cluster.

faq.q: How much do rooms cost at Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit?
faq.a: Rooms start from approx. THB 1,500/night for a Cozy Twin (23 sqm). A Quartier King (27 sqm) runs around THB 1,700 and a Deluxe King (32 sqm) approximately THB 2,200. Rates vary with season and package; always compare platforms before booking.

faq.q: Which BTS station is closest to Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit?
faq.a: BTS Phrom Phong is the nearest station, approximately 850 metres from the hotel. Because the hotel sits in a residential cul-de-sac with no direct public transport, most guests use Grab or a metered taxi — around 10–12 minutes and THB 80–100.

faq.q: Does Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit have free parking?
faq.a: Yes. The hotel provides free on-site parking for guests, which is a practical benefit for those driving themselves or transporting a patient who cannot use public transport.

faq.q: Who is Quartier by Montraj Sukhumvit best suited for?
faq.a: It suits anyone attending Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital — whether as a patient or a companion — above all. It also works well for couples or solo travellers wanting a quiet, design-conscious base in the Phrom Phong–Thonglor area, and for guests travelling with pets (pet-friendly policy).
